title: Mr. Nanguo and the Yu Ensemble
text:
The philosopher Han Fei tells this story. King Xuan of Qi loved music played on the yu, a mouth organ made of bamboo pipes, and he especially loved to hear it played by a great ensemble. He kept three hundred players, who always performed together.

A man called Mr. Nanguo asked to join. He could not play the yu at all, but he saw that among three hundred musicians, nobody would notice one who only pretended. The king was pleased to have another player and gave him the same pay and rations as the rest, which were generous. For years Mr. Nanguo sat with the ensemble, holding his instrument to his lips, swaying in time and collecting his wages.

Then King Xuan died, and his son, King Min, came to the throne. The new king also loved the yu, but he had different taste. He preferred to hear the players one at a time, each performing for him alone.

When Mr. Nanguo heard of the new arrangement, he slipped away and fled before his turn came.
lesson: A large group can hide someone who does not contribute, but only until each person's work is seen on its own. Make individual contributions visible.
people: Mr. Nanguo, King Xuan of Qi, King Min of Qi
source: Han Feizi, Inner Collections of Sayings, Upper Series (Nei Chu Shuo Shang)
